guard: partial: only millisecond Date.now() entropy, no os.tmpdir() indirection, no O_EXCL/exclusive-create flag and no restrictive file mode; a locally co-resident attacker who pre-creates a symlink at the predictable /tmp/values-<ms>.yaml path before the call is made can redirect the write to an arbitrary path the server process can write to (same pattern repeats in the useTemplate code path at lines 269-271 for /tmp/values-*.yaml and /tmp/helm-template-*.yaml)
why: Every install with an inline `values` object (or useTemplate mode) writes attacker-supplied YAML through a predictably-named temp file in a shared world-writable directory with no exclusive-create/O_EXCL and no restrictive mode, which is the classic TOCTOU symlink-race pattern for insecure temp files (CWE-377); exploitability requires a second local actor able to pre-plant a symlink at the guessed path, which I cannot confirm is present in a given deployment.

the 'set' operation only ever runs `kubectl config use-context <contextName>` where contextName is required to already appear in the output of `kubectl config get-contexts -o name` (checked just before use), so an attacker cannot inject an arbitrary flag-shaped or credential-redirecting value as the context name.

why: This tool is the only one of the temp-file writers that added a restrictive mode, which meaningfully reduces confidentiality exposure of the resulting file's contents, but it does not close the underlying symlink pre-plant/TOCTOU path since no exclusive-create flag is used and the filename remains guessable; kept at Tier B given the partial mitigation and the local-attacker precondition.
